The programmes

Choose what you will build.

Every AI system stands on four layers. Choose the chips it runs on, the devices it lives in, the machines it moves or the intelligence inside. Each four-year B.Tech follows the same approach: build a working project every semester.

Book a campus visit

Compare the four B.Tech courses

The chip · Electronics Engineering (VLSI Design and Technology)

Design the chips inside phones, cars and AI systems. A good fit if you enjoy logic, puzzles and precise work. Explore careers in chip design, verification and physical design.

Explore VLSI Design and Technology

The device · Electronics and Computer Engineering

Put circuits, software and AI together in smart devices such as EV chargers and medical monitors. A good fit if both electronics and computing interest you. Explore careers in embedded systems, firmware and product engineering.

Explore Electronics and Computer Engineering

The machine · Robotics and Artificial Intelligence

Build robots and drones that sense and move. A good fit if you want your code to move things in the real world. Explore careers in robotics, automation and machine perception.

Explore Robotics and Artificial Intelligence

The intelligence · CSE (Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning)

Build systems that learn from data, make decisions and generate content. A good fit if you enjoy mathematics, data and software. Explore careers in applied AI, machine learning and data science.

Explore CSE (AI and Machine Learning)

The company · BBA and MBA

Learn how to finance a product, source its parts, reach customers and grow a business. Work alongside future engineers and use AI as a business tool.

Explore management courses

For those who want the detail

The four B.Tech programmes share a project-based learning model. Projects increase in difficulty and lead to a final semester of supervised engineering work. Individual practical assessments record the skills each student can demonstrate independently.
